messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty SEV2 - redis-prod-acceptqueue firing on service `redis-prod` (alert: redis.acceptqueue.depth > 5000)

lina: ack'd. I'm on-call for the next 30m. pinging @sam and @raj-db for help. link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345

sam: I see acceptqueue trending up in grafana (https://grafana.internal/boards/cache). 5xxs from cache-backed endpoints started ~2m ago. Rolling error spike at 30rps -> 5xx.

raj: pulling metrics from host. running quick checks.

raj: ```
$ redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 INFO clients | grep connected_clients
connected_clients:10120
$ redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 INFO | grep maxclients
maxclients:10000
``` 

raj: Oof, connected_clients ~= maxclients. That's why accept queue is growing.

alex: /cc @db-sre - also seeing pgbouncer queues on primary DB because some requests that fallback to DB are increasing. Noticed application retry storm on cache misses.

sam: any recent deploys? I don't see anything in releasebot in the last hour.

lina: no deploys from my side. Could be surge from a cron or downstream job.

raj: quick mitigation options:
- increase redis maxclients on host (risky, kernel limits)
- scale up redis instances (add replica, start new pod)
- apply traffic-level throttle / fail-open to reduce connections

lina: let's avoid changing kernel limits. Plan: scale redis horizontally + block noisy job if we identify it.

sam: starting scale via k8s: `kubectl scale sts redis-prod --replicas=3` (we currently have 1 primary + 2 replicas desired but only 1 ready). Pushing now.

sam: ```
scaled statefulset "redis-prod" to 3
# waiting for pods to come up
``` 

raj: while that finishes, suggest enabling short-term connection health limit at the API edge. @jess can you flip the feature-flag that reduces per-request cache concurrency? It will 429 some non-critical background traffic.

jess: on it. toggling flag `edge.cache.concurrency.limiter` -> 20 for background routes.

jess: ```
POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle
{"flag":"edge.cache.concurrency.limiter","value":20,"env":"prod","actor":"jess"}
# response 200
``` 

jess: applied. Watching results now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: redis acceptqueue depth dropped from 6k -> 1.2k in last 45s (grafana). 5xxs reduced but not gone.

raj: new redis pod came up and joined cluster, connections migrated -> connected_clients now 4800.

raj: ```
connected_clients:4820
``` 

alex: DB pgbouncer queue dropped too, looks like the retry pressure subsided. Customer impact: some user-facing requests were failing with 500 for ~3 minutes. No major outage, but noisy for a small subset (payment cache lookups). We should notify CS and post an incident note.

lina: creating incident doc in ops-docs and pinging CS. link: https://confluence.internal/ops/incidents/redis-acceptqueue-1759876543

jess: did PagerDuty escalate? incident-bot said page to SRE and DB, but no PD escalation yet.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: acknowledged by lina, no automatic escalation (PD policy: 15m quiet window). Logged incident ID PD12345.

sam: let's also add a temporary rate-limit on the specific payment cache route to prevent future spikes. I'll open a PR for a 2s debounce + 429 for non-critical callers.

raj: follow-up action items:
- (short) add circuit-breaker on payment cache route (sam)
- (short) verify kernel ulimit and restart plan if we need to increase maxclients (raj)
- (mid) add alert to correlate pgbouncer queue + redis connected_clients (alex)
- (post) postmortem with traffic analysis and root cause (lina)

alex: agree. Customer impact assessment: ~0.03% of requests produced 500s for 3 minutes, primarily payments internal reruns. No data loss.

jess: I've notified CS and bumped priority for the postmortem. CS will reach out to affected customers if needed. :white_check_mark:

lina: handing off to @raj-db for watch. I'll stay online for 10m then hand to next oncall (jess).

raj: ack. I'll monitor logs and metrics for next 40m and start the kernel/limits checklist. If we see >80% of maxclients again, we'll take DB read-fallback and escalate.

sam: sanity check: any config changes we committed? None. I'll keep an eye on retries and open the PR for the rate-limit.

jess: noted. setting follow-up reminders and adding runbook link in the incident doc.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident note appended to PD12345 by lina. Next reminder in 15m.

lina: thanks team. marking as stable for now but not closing PD. handoff in 10.

raj: :thumbsup:
